title: Setting up a development environment locally
author: Peter
content:
The first step is to create a directory somewhere on your local machine.  If you are intending to make multiple projects then it probably makes sense  to have a top level directory (e.g. called Django projects) and then create a sub-directory for each project.

Navigate into the directory just created and create a Python Virtual Environment.  I save the environment in the directory itself.  A virtual environment is not essential but I highly recommend doing so for each project as the requirements for each of your projects is likely to be specific so you can tailor each environment to suit your project.

This command will create a virtual environment called virtenv:

python3 -m venv virtenv

Start VS Code (or whatever editor you use by choice) and open the project directory.  If you have VS Code installed this can be done by entering the project directory in a terminal session and entering:

code .

Before we set up git we are going to create a .gitignore file to specify which items we don’t want to be source controlled by git.  Use the sample and edit as appropriate.  Make sure the name of the virtual environment you created for the project is included in the ‘Environments’ section.

Start using git

Hit the ‘Source control’ icon on the left of the VS Code screen and then hit ‘initialise repository’.
